title.en: Lok Sabha, Money Bills and the Speaker

text.en: Every adult citizen aged 18 and above who is registered can vote for the Lok Sabha. It is the one House directly elected by the people, so it has the last word on money.

The members of the Lok Sabha are directly elected from constituencies based on population, and the Election Commission conducts the polls.
Universal adult franchise applies, so all registered citizens above 18 years vote.
Only the Lok Sabha can introduce a Money Bill, and Rajya Sabha can neither amend nor reject it.
If the Rajya Sabha fails to pass it within 14 days, the bill is deemed passed, and the Lok Sabha need not consider the Rajya Sabha's amendments.
The Lok Sabha elects the President and Vice-President along with the Rajya Sabha, and has equal power in constitutional amendments and impeachment.
A no-confidence motion can be introduced only in the Lok Sabha, and if it is passed the Prime Minister and the Council of Ministers must resign.
The Speaker is elected by the members and presides over the House, and also over a joint sitting of both Houses.
He decides whether a bill is a Money Bill, and he continues in office even after dissolution until a new Speaker is elected.
When the Speaker is absent the Deputy Speaker presides, except when a resolution to remove the Speaker is being considered.
Parliament has three sessions, the Budget Session from February to May, the Monsoon Session from July to September, and the Winter Session from November to December.
Parliament makes laws, oversees the administration, passes the Budget, airs public grievances, and can change the boundaries of states.
It can also remove judges of the Supreme Court and High Courts, the Chief Election Commissioner and the CAG by the constitutional procedure.
Tamil Nadu sends 39 members to the Lok Sabha and 18 to the Rajya Sabha.

problem.en: What is a Money Bill and how is it passed?

text.en: It deals with taxation and government money, and needs the President's approval to be introduced.

why.en: Only the Lok Sabha can introduce it.

text.en: The Rajya Sabha cannot amend or reject it but may take 14 days.

why.en: It then goes to the President.

text.en: If it does not pass within 14 days, it is treated as passed.

why.en: The Lok Sabha may ignore the Rajya Sabha's suggestions.

prompt.en: State the powers and role of the Speaker.

requiredIdeas.en: Continues after dissolution until a new Speaker

commonMisconceptions.en: Saying the Vice-President presides over Lok Sabha

points.en: Lok Sabha: direct election, adult franchise at 18.
Money Bill: only Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha has 14 days.
No-confidence motion only in Lok Sabha.
Speaker decides Money Bill, presides over joint sittings.
